title: Rocket.Chat Mobile
description: Build a channel/message mobile demo with a small DDP client, typed mapping, persistent offline state, and an explicit endpoint configuration boundary.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend Rocket.Chat Mobile while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace channel/chatmessage models, seeded data, and unread display in its named source files.
Explain and trace socket abstraction, connect/session, method ids, ping/pong, timeout and close in its named source files.
Explain and trace tochannels/tomessages, filtering, unread counts, optimistic append in its named source files.
Explain and trace expo_public_chat_url, secure websocket validation, `.example` rejection, idle status in its named source files.
Explain and trace asyncstorage adapter, load/save effects, context actions, and optimistic state in its named source files.
Explain and trace tab shell, selected channel, offline banner, reconnect control, shared components, and status rendering in its named source files.
Explain and trace fake socket assertions, endpoint test cases, dependency and provider review in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
